title: Quantum Query Advantage Requires Space
summary: Hao, Huang, and Liu (STOC'26) recently showed that optimal quantum query complexity may require large workspace even for short-output problems, and asked whether a quantum query advantage over classical computation can itself require space. We resolve this question by exhibiting an explicit total Boolean function with quantum query complexity $Q=\widetildeΘ(M)$, and randomized query complexity $R=Θ(M^{21/20})$, whereas, for every fixed $0<η<1/100$ and $S\le O(M^{1/100-η})$, its $S$-space quantum query complexity satisfies $Q_S=ω(M^{21/20})$.
